final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and largely conceded the core compliance defects. The response is a reframing of the same record, not an evidentiary update. That reframing usefully narrows the claim: the Actor no longer defends a clean resolution of the disclosure issue and instead argues for a qualified release-level certification theory. But that narrower position is still insufficient for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely a reporting nuance; it is the compliance predicate itself. The governing policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless they are resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Available admissible evidence shows a target miss in a segment named in a renewal success plan, an open legal question about required disclosure, and no evidence of disclosure or approved risk acceptance. On that record, the certification action remains noncompliant, even if there is some admissible support for aggregate operational readiness.
remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence still shows the enterprise refund workflow misses target and is tied to a named customer commitment, which supports materiality under the stated policy.
There is still no admissible evidence of pre-launch disclosure of the limitation in the model card.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved limitation before launch.
The legal review ticket remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved at decision time.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation.
